---
title: "Construct the W_ah Design Matrix from Phased Haplotype Genotypes"
---

## Construct the W_ah Design Matrix from Phased Haplotype Genotypes {.unnumbered}


### Description

Build the multi-allelic design matrix $W_{\alpha h}$ (Da, 2015) from
phased haplotype calls. The matrix is the input expected by
<code>run_bayesr</code> and <code>run_bayesa</code>.



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>construct_wah_matrix(
  hap_matrix,
  colnames,
  allele_freq_filtered = NULL,
  reference_structure = NULL,
  drop_baseline = TRUE
)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="hap_matrix">hap_matrix</code></td>
<td>
Integer matrix of phased haplotype allele codes, with
dimensions <code>n x 2*blocks</code>. Coerced to integer storage internally.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="colnames">colnames</code></td>
<td>
Column names of <code>hap_matrix</code> (length <code>2*blocks</code>).
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="allele_freq_filtered">allele_freq_filtered</code></td>
<td>
A <code>data.frame</code> with columns
<code>haplotype</code>, <code>allele</code>, and <code>freq</code>. Required for the
training set; pass <code>NULL</code> for the test set.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="reference_structure">reference_structure</code></td>
<td>
The full return value of a prior training-set
call. Required for the test set; pass <code>NULL</code> for the training set.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="drop_baseline">drop_baseline</code></td>
<td>
If <code>TRUE</code> (default) the most-frequent allele per
block is dropped to ensure full rank.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Details

The haplotype matrix has dimensions <code>n x 2*blocks</code>: each individual
contributes two phased copies per block. Column names encode block
identity (e.g. <code>hap_1_1</code> and <code>hap_1_1_1</code> are the two copies of
block 1).

For each block, the most-frequent allele (the baseline, dropped when
<code>drop_baseline = TRUE</code>) is removed for identifiability; the remaining
alleles become columns of $W_{\alpha h}$ encoded with the Da (2015)
rule. A frequency-weighted projection enforces the sum-to-zero
constraint $E[W_k] = 0$.

<strong>W_ah encoding (Da, 2015).</strong>
For individual $i$ with phased alleles $(A_i, A_j)$ at haplotype
block $h$, the column corresponding to non-baseline allele $k$
(with population frequency $p_k$) is coded as:


<dl>
<dt>Homozygous ($A_i = A_j = k$):</dt><dd>
$W_{\alpha h}^{(k)} = -2(1 - p_k)$
</dd>
<dt>Heterozygous ($A_i = k$ or $A_j = k$):</dt><dd>
$W_{\alpha h}^{(k)} = -(1 - 2p_k)$
</dd>
<dt>Absent ($A_i \neq k$ and $A_j \neq k$):</dt><dd>
$W_{\alpha h}^{(k)} = 2p_k$
</dd>
</dl>

Rare alleles receive larger absolute deviations; common alleles receive
smaller deviations. The population column-mean is zero by construction,
ensuring the additive effects sum to zero across individuals.

<strong>Cross-validation / train-test split workflow:</strong>


<ol>
<li> Build the matrix on the <em>training</em> set: pass
<code>allele_freq_filtered = &lt;freq_table&gt;</code> and
<code>reference_structure = NULL</code>.

</li>
<li> Build the matrix on the <em>test</em> set with the training
structure: pass the entire training-set return value as
<code>reference_structure</code> and leave <code>allele_freq_filtered = NULL</code>.
This guarantees the test matrix has identical columns and the same
baseline alleles as the training matrix.

</li></ol>



### Value

A list with three elements:


<dl>
<dt><code>W_ah</code></dt><dd>Numeric matrix <code>n x p</code> with named columns
<code>&lt;block&gt;_allele&lt;k&gt;</code>.
</dd>
<dt><code>allele_info</code></dt><dd>Data frame describing each retained column
(<code>allele_id, block, allele, freq</code>).
</dd>
<dt><code>dropped_alleles</code></dt><dd>Data frame of baseline alleles that were
removed; empty if <code>drop_baseline = FALSE</code>.
</dd>
</dl>



### References

Da, Y. (2015). Multi-allelic haplotype model based on genetic
partition for genomic prediction and variance component estimation
using SNP markers. <em>BMC Genetics</em>, 16(1), 144.
[doi:10.1186/s12863-015-0301-1](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12863-015-0301-1)



### See Also

<code>run_bayesr</code>, <code>run_bayesa</code>



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masbayes")

d        <- load_data("small")
block_id <- attr(d$mh, "block_id")

# Training set -- pass d$allele_freq (required when reference_structure is NULL)
hap_tr  <- d$mh[d$train_idx, ]
train   <- construct_wah_matrix(hap_tr, block_id, d$allele_freq)
W_train <- train$W_ah

# Test set: reuse the training allele structure to keep columns aligned
hap_te <- d$mh[d$test_idx, ]
test   <- construct_wah_matrix(hap_te, block_id,
                               reference_structure = train)
W_test <- test$W_ah
stopifnot(ncol(W_train) == ncol(W_test))




```
